case_name: R. R. Parekh v High Court of Gujarat and another
respondent:
High Court of Gujarat and another
Supreme Court of India

12 July 2016
Civil Appeal Nos 6116-6117 of 2016 [Arising out of SLP (C) Nos. 34674-34675 of 2012]
The Judgment was delivered by : D.Y. Chandrachud, J.
1. Leave granted.
2. These proceedings arise from a judgment of the High Court of Gujarat dated 23 February 2012 in an application filed by the Appellant challenging the punishment of dismissal imposed upon him upon a disciplinary inquiry. The Division Bench of the Gujarat High Court found that the charges against the Appellant have been established in one (but not the second) of two disciplinary inquiries in respect of his conduct as a judicial officer in the district judiciary. In view of its findings, the High Court declined to interfere with the punishment of dismissal. That has given rise to these proceedings.

facts: The proceedings arise from a judgment of the High Court of Gujarat dated 23 February 2012 in an application filed by the Appellant challenging the punishment of dismissal imposed upon him upon a disciplinary inquiry.
The Appellant was recruited as a Civil Judge (Junior Division) and Judicial Magistrate in 1981 in the judicial service of the State of Gujarat.
Two criminal cases involving offences punishable under Section 135 of the Customs Act 1962 and the Imports & Exports (Control) Act 1947 were tried by him.
In Criminal Case 1293 of 1995, the Appellant delivered a judgment on 22 January 1997 convicting the accused, but awarded a sentence of imprisonment less than the minimum prescribed by Section 135.
Fourteen accused were alleged to be involved in the smuggling of 275 silver slabs of a value of Rs. 5,86,50,620/-.
The Appellant was charged with a dereliction of duty and of acting in a manner unbecoming of a judicial officer.
The Inquiry Officer exonerated the Appellant.
The Disciplinary Committee came to the conclusion that there was insufficient evidence to hold the Appellant guilty of an oblique motive or corrupt practice.
issues: What is the appropriate punishment for a judicial officer who awards less than the minimum sentence prescribed by law?
Is the Appellant's conduct in awarding lenient sentences in two criminal cases a breach of his duties as a judicial officer?
Can the Appellant be held liable for misconduct and dismissed from service based on the findings of the Disciplinary Committee?
petitioner_arguments: The Appellant denied the charges in his reply to the chargesheet.
The Appellant argued that even if an error was committed by him in awarding less than the prescribed sentence, this was of a bona fide nature.
The Appellant claimed that he had passed an order of conviction and sentence without looking at the provisions of the Customs Act 1962.
respondent_arguments: The Respondent argued that the Appellant's conduct in awarding lenient sentences in two criminal cases was a breach of his duties as a judicial officer.
The Respondent claimed that the Appellant had failed to consider the provisions of the Customs Act 1962 and had passed an order of conviction and sentence without looking at the statute.
The Respondent argued that the Appellant's conduct was not totally bona fide and proposed that this should be considered when the case of the Appellant for promotion arose in future.
court_reasoning: The Court held that as a seasoned judicial officer who was in service since 1981, the Appellant would be aware about the basic principles of sentencing.
The Court rejected the explanation of the Appellant that even if an error was committed by him in awarding less than the prescribed sentence, this was of a bona fide nature.
The Court found it difficult to accept that as a judicial officer, the Appellant had passed an order of conviction and sentence without looking at the provisions.

The Court held that an inference could be drawn on the basis of material with regard to the existence of an oblique motive since neither a sufficient nor reasonable explanation was provided by the Appellant.
holding: The Full Court of the High Court resolved that the charges against the Appellant were proved and decided to dismiss the Appellant from service.
The State Government by a notification dated 14 July 2009 dismissed the Appellant from service.
